subject: Maths
title: Quadratic sequences
subtitle: Sequences · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can find the nth term of a quadratic sequence.

key_vocab.definition: A quadratic sequence has a constant second difference. The nth term has the form an² + bn + c.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can find the nth term of a quadratic sequence.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: quadratic sequence -- A quadratic sequence has a constant second difference. The nth term has the form an² + bn + c.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Find second differences (= 2a). Subtract an² from each term to get a linear sequence, then find b and c.
un = an² + bn + c
2a = second difference; then find b and c from the remainder

Key examples:
  ✓ 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ... has nth term n²  (second diff = 2)
  ✓ 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ... has 2nd diff = 2  (quadratic)
  ✓ Second difference = 2a, so if 2nd diff = 6 then a = 3  (finding a)
  ✗ 2, 5, 8, 11, ... is quadratic  (constant first diff = arithmetic)
  ✗ Second difference = a  (second difference = 2a)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – finding the nth term
  Find the nth term of 3, 8, 15, 24, 35, ...
  First differences: 5, 7, 9, 11. Second differences: 2, 2, 2. So 2a = 2, a = 1
  Subtract n²: 3−1=2, 8−4=4, 15−9=6, 24−16=8. Linear sequence: 2, 4, 6, 8 = 2n
  nth term = n² + 2n
  n² + 2n
  (Check: when n=1: 1+2=3. When n=2: 4+4=8. Correct!)

Example 2 – second difference not 2
  Find the nth term of 2, 8, 18, 32, 50, ...
  First diff: 6, 10, 14, 18. Second diff: 4, 4, 4. So 2a = 4, a = 2
  Subtract 2n²: 2−2=0, 8−8=0, 18−18=0. All zeros!
  nth term = 2n²
  2n²
  (When subtracting an² gives all zeros, b = c = 0.)

sections.title: Recognising quadratic sequences
sections.content:
Show these are quadratic by finding second differences.

(a) 1, 4, 9, 16, 25
(b) 2, 6, 12, 20, 30
(c) 3, 12, 27, 48, 75
(d) 0, 3, 10, 21, 36

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Find the nth term and use it.

(a) 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ... nth term?
(b) Using your answer to (a), find the 10th term.
(c) 2, 9, 20, 35, 54, ... nth term?
(d) Is 100 in the sequence n² + 2n?
(e) Find the 20th term of 3n² − n + 1.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ A quadratic sequence has a constant second difference
✗ If first differences are constant, the sequence is quadratic
✓ Second difference = 2a where a is the coefficient of n²
✗ The second difference equals the coefficient of n²
✓ After subtracting an², the remainder forms a linear sequence

teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Recognising quadratic sequences:
  (a) 1st diff: 3,5,7,9; 2nd diff: 2,2,2
  (b) 1st diff: 4,6,8,10; 2nd diff: 2,2,2
  (c) 1st diff: 9,15,21,27; 2nd diff: 6,6,6
  (d) 1st diff: 3,7,11,15; 2nd diff: 4,4,4

Simple nth terms:
  (a) n²
  (b) n² + 3
  (c) n² − 1
  (d) 2n²

With linear part:
  (a) n² + 2n
  (b) n² + 2n − 1
  (c) n² + 3n
  (d) 2n² + n + 2

Harder nth terms:
  (a) 2n² + 3n + 1
  (b) 2n² − 1 (check: should be 2n²+2n−3... recalc)
  (c) 2n² − 2
  (d) 2n² + n + 2

Mixed problems:
